Class RejectShell

java.lang.Object
org.casserole.ssh.shell.RejectShell
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.apache.sshd.server.command.Command, org.apache.sshd.server.command.CommandDirectErrorStreamAware, org.apache.sshd.server.command.CommandDirectInputStreamAware, org.apache.sshd.server.command.CommandDirectOutputStreamAware, org.apache.sshd.server.command.CommandDirectStreamsAware, org.apache.sshd.server.command.CommandLifecycle
public class RejectShell extends Object implements org.apache.sshd.server.command.Command
The RejectShell class is an SSH command that writes one red line and then ends the channel. The factory returns this command when a login is refused. The command does not open stored chat memory for the user. The constructor stores the reason text. start(ChannelSession, Environment) writes that text in red. The method then asks the exit callback to leave with status 1. // @aa-sdd L40 aa-sdd-source-prose.md#RejectShell

    • start

      public void start(org.apache.sshd.server.channel.ChannelSession channel, org.apache.sshd.server.Environment env) throws IOException
      The method writes the reason in red and then ends the channel with status 1. A missing output stream skips the write. A write failure is ignored. A missing exit callback skips the status.
      Specified by:
      start in interface org.apache.sshd.server.command.CommandLifecycle
      Parameters:
      channel - The channel is the SSH channel that started this command.
      env - The environment is the channel environment. The method does not read it.
